Present: Mr. Kulwinder Singh, Advocate for  Mr. S.S. Sarwara, Advocate for the petitioner.
Ms. Navreet Kaur Barnala, AAG Punjab.

Mr. M.S. Bhatti, Advocate for respondent No.2.
 *

** *
HARPREET SINGH BRAR J. (ORAL)

This petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking quashing of FIR No.114 dated 18.04.2022 registered under Sections 406, 420 and 506 of Indian Penal Code at Police Station Zirakpur, Tehsil Dera Bassi, District SAS Nagar and all subsequent proceedings arising therefrom in view of the compromise dated 17.05.2023 (Annexure P-2).
2.

The FIR registered on the statement of complainant- respondent No. 2 on the allegations that petitioner is a co-worker with her husband and he cheated them for an amount of Rs.12,00,000/- on the pretext of deputing their son at government job and when they demanded their money back,
petitioner started abusing them and threatened to kill them.
3. Keeping in view the fact that the parties have entered into a compromise, they were directed to appear before the trial Court/Illaqa Magistrate for getting their statements recorded in support of the compromise.
1 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:161913 2023:PHHC:161913

In pursuance of the direction, a report has been received from Judicial Magistrate Ist Class, Dera Bassi, stating that the compromise Pardeep Kumar vs State Of Punjab And Another on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89948672/
1 arrived at between the parties is without any pressure or coercion from any one and the same is genuine one.
4.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Advocate General, Punjab, on instructions from the Investigating Officer and learned counsel for respondent No.2 admitted the factum of compromise and submitted that in case, the parties have indeed settled their dispute, the State would have no objection to the quashing of the FIR, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the record with their able assistance.
6. The parties have arrived at a compromise and settled their dispute.
A compromise not only brings peace and harmony between the parties to a dispute, but also restores tranquility in the society.

After considering the nature of offences allegedly committed and the fact that both the parties have amicably settled their dispute, continuance of criminal prosecution would be an exercise in futility,
as the chances of ultimate conviction are bleak.

A two Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shakunta Sawhney (Mrs) Vs. Kaushalya (Mrs.) and others (1980) 1 SCC 63, speaking through Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer, has held as under:-
"4. ....The finest hour of justice arrives propitiously when parties, despite falling apart, bury the hatchet and weave a sense of fellowship or reunion....."
7.

sentences.text:
A perusal of the report sent by Judicial Magistrate Ist Class, Dera Bassi, indicates that respondent No.2, who is the complainant in the present FIR has made the statement in terms of the compromise effected between the 2 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:161913 2023:PHHC:161839 parties.
8.

Consequently, keeping in view the fact that the dispute has been amicably settled and in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Narinder Singh and others vs. State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466 and Ramgopal and another Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 2021 SCC OnLine SC 834 and Full Bench of this Court in Kulwinder Singh Vs. State of Punjab 2007 (3) RCR (Crl.) 1052, this petition is allowed and FIR No.114 dated 18.04.2022 registered under Sections 406,
420 and 506 of Indian Penal Code at Police Station Zirakpur, Tehsil Dera Bassi, SAS Nagar, District SAS Nagar and all subsequent proceedings arising out of the same are quashed qua the petitioner only.
